title: cAST: Enhancing Code Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Structural Chunking via Abstract Syntax Tree
what_they_did: Proposed recursive AST node splitting and merging for code generation on RepoEval and SWE-bench
difference_from_this_study: Evaluates synthetic code generation rather than human-annotated requirement-to-code evidence retrieval and does not isolate the orthogonal effect of hierarchical context headers via a 2x2 factorial design

title: How Does Chunking Affect Retrieval-Augmented Code Completion? A Controlled Empirical Study
what_they_did: Empirically compared fixed-size and semantic chunking granularities for repository-level code completion
difference_from_this_study: Focuses on next-token completion perplexity rather than evidence retrieval against formal requirements and does not audit fallback penetration in top-k retrieved results

title: CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages
what_they_did: Introduced bimodal pre-trained representations for NL-PL matching and semantic code search
difference_from_this_study: Evaluates standalone bi-encoder retrieval over isolated function-docstring pairs rather than multi-tier bi-encoder plus cross-encoder reranking over multi-file repositories

title: UniXcoder: Unified Cross-Modal Pre-training for Code Representation
what_they_did: Proposed unified cross-modal pre-training incorporating AST flattening for code retrieval and generation
difference_from_this_study: Operates on individual method snippets with docstrings rather than repository-level chunking with fallback audits and statistical hypothesis testing

title: BGE M3-Embedding: Multi-Lingual Multi-Functionality Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings Through Self-Knowledge Distillation
what_they_did: Developed multi-lingual multi-granularity dense representations supporting dense lexical and multi-vector search
difference_from_this_study: Proposes a general-purpose embedding model without empirical evaluation of code chunking boundary integrity or cross-language OOP vs JSX fragmentation

title: C-Pack: Packaged Resources to Advance General Chinese and Multilingual Embedding
what_they_did: Introduced BGE re-ranker cross-encoders trained on hard negatives for general text and code reranking
difference_from_this_study: Does not investigate how cross-encoder attention weights interact with AST method-level truncation versus line-based sliding windows

title: CoSTV: Two-Stage Code Search with Program Simplification and Model Distillation
what_they_did: Applied a two-stage retrieve-then-rerank pipeline with code simplification for efficiency in code search
difference_from_this_study: Focuses on accelerating cross-encoder inference for natural language queries rather than evaluating AST syntactic integrity and context headers on real-world multi-language repos

title: RepoCoder: Repository-Level Code Completion Through Iterative Retrieval and Generation
what_they_did: Proposed an iterative retrieval-generation framework using sliding line windows and similarity-based retrieval across repository files
difference_from_this_study: Relies strictly on fixed line-based sliding windows without investigating AST syntactic boundaries or factorial isolation of context header metadata

title: RepoBench: Benchmarking Complete Code Generation with Repository-Level Context
what_they_did: Established a repository-level benchmark evaluating retrieval and completion across in-file and cross-file contexts
difference_from_this_study: Focuses on code completion targets rather than requirement-to-code evidence ranking under dual-annotator Cranfield pooling standards

title: CrossCodeEval: A Diverse and Multilingual Benchmark for Cross-File Code Completion
what_they_did: Constructed a cross-file benchmark highlighting the necessity of cross-file context for code completion
difference_from_this_study: Evaluates language model completion rather than information retrieval ranking metrics (NDCG MRR MAP) across chunking paradigms

title: Recovering Traceability Links between Code and Documentation
what_they_did: Pioneered information retrieval methods (vector space model and probabilistic model) for recovering traceability links between requirements and code
difference_from_this_study: Uses classic bag-of-words IR on coarse file/class granularity rather than modern dense neural retrieval and cross-encoder reranking over AST chunks

title: Triad: Automated Traceability Recovery Based on Biterm-Enhanced Deduction of Transitive Links Among Artifacts
what_they_did: Developed transitive link deduction to recover trace links between natural language requirements and software source code
difference_from_this_study: Addresses issue-to-commit and requirement-to-class transitive graphs rather than fine-grained chunk-level evidence retrieval for skill requirements

title: Identifying Skills of Open Source Developers: An Automated Approach
what_they_did: Extracted developer skills from GitHub repositories using keyword matching and topic modeling over repository commits
difference_from_this_study: Uses repository-level tag aggregation rather than semantic RAG retrieval of concrete source code evidence for specific mandatory requirement items

title: CodeSearchNet Challenge: Evaluating the State of Semantic Code Search
what_they_did: Curated 2 million (comment code) pairs across six languages as a standard benchmark for semantic code search
difference_from_this_study: Samples isolated individual methods without class or package enclosing context and without evaluating chunking trade-offs on full multi-file repositories

title: Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation: A Survey with Focus on Repository-Level Approaches
what_they_did: Surveyed repository-level retrieval-augmented code generation categorizing chunking retrieval and generation strategies
difference_from_this_study: Provides a literature taxonomy without empirical factorial benchmarking of syntactic boundary preservation versus retrieval accuracy

title: Analyzing and Detecting Traceability Link Evolution in Software Repositories
what_they_did: Analyzed how requirement-to-code trace links evolve across Git commit histories using machine learning
difference_from_this_study: Focuses on historical link evolution rather than multi-stage RAG chunking and context header effects for requirement evidence matching

title: Practical Code RAG at Scale: Task-Aware Retrieval Design Choices under Compute Budgets
what_they_did: Evaluated code retrieval design choices under compute budgets finding line chunking matches syntax-aware splitting
difference_from_this_study: Evaluates general code completion retrieval across context budgets without 2x2 factorial isolation of hierarchical headers for human-labeled requirements

title: Revisiting Code Search in a Two-Stage Paradigm
what_they_did: Proposed TOSS two-stage recall and rerank framework for code search using cross-encoders
difference_from_this_study: Evaluates method-level code search queries rather than repository-level requirement-to-code evidence chunks with AST fallback audits

title: The Measurement of Observer Agreement for Categorical Data
what_they_did: Introduced standard benchmark intervals for interpreting Cohen's Kappa agreement coefficients
difference_from_this_study: Foundational biostatistics methodology establishing standard agreement categories

title: Individual Comparisons by Ranking Methods
what_they_did: Proposed the non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired continuous data
difference_from_this_study: Foundational non-parametric statistical testing method

title: A Simple Sequentially Rejective Multiple Test Procedure
what_they_did: Introduced the step-down Holm-Bonferroni method controlling family-wise error rate under arbitrary dependence
difference_from_this_study: Foundational multiple testing correction procedure

title: Retrieval Evaluation with Incomplete Information
what_they_did: Proposed binary preference (bpref) metric evaluating retrieval when relevance judgments are incomplete
difference_from_this_study: Foundational information retrieval metric for unjudged pooled items
